messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Multiple ELB frontends in us-west-2 reporting 502/handshake failures and elevated error-rate. Auto-paging oncall.

sara-oncall: I'm on-call and looking. seeing a spike in 502s from our edge ELBs (~18% p95) per Datadog. Thanks for the page.

ajay: pinging AWS status & health dashboards. Also can someone check TGW route tables for any recent route updates? we've seen similar symptoms with route leaks before.

lee: can confirm increased TLS handshake timeouts in the edge logs. backend connections look OK from our side. suspect asymmetric routing/egress path.

sara-oncall: running quick checks:
```bash
# curl direct to ELB
curl -I https://api.redwood-inference.internal --silent --max-time 5
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```

sara-oncall: also pulled health for target group:
```bash
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123:targetgroup/tg-front/abc
# some targets showing initial or unhealthy states, intermittent
```

maria: Support note: customers in NA experiencing errors on infer endpoints; latency surges too. Initial impact estimate: roughly 12-20% of requests failing with 502, higher p95 latencies for retried requests. Triage to customer-facing comms in 30m if unresolved.

ajay: saw a flurry of TGW route propagation events around +800s ago from CloudTrail. Could be a route leak from partner VPC causing return-paths to go through the wrong AZ. Asking infra-net to confirm.

ops-bot: @infra-networking created incident ticket INC-2026-1789 and notified aws-support. Route propagation logs attached.

lee: to mitigate quick: can we shift traffic weight on the R53/weighted routing policy away from problematic AZs / ELBs? We have capacity in us-east-1 and eu-west-1.

sara-oncall: starting weighted steering now: shifting 35% -> us-east-1, 15% -> eu-west-1. Will monitor error-rate and latency.

support-shift: Heads-up to sales and SRE on customer-impact list: matrix shows top 5 tenants with most errors. Liaising with CS for targeted apologies + workaround steps.

ajay: AWS response: they've opened a ticket and are investigating possible TGW->TransitGateway route propagation anomalies in us-west-2. They requested packet captures on our side and BGP route tables.

sara-oncall: uploaded tcpdump from edge-nat instance to the ticket. Noted visible retransmits and RSTs to certain AZ egress IPs.

maria: Customer comms draft: "Experiencing elevated 502s in us-west-2 due to regional network routing disruption; traffic being shifted to alternate regions. We're monitoring and will update every 15 minutes." Approve? :thumbsup:

lee: +1 send. Also putting in an emergency rollback to pin critical customers to dedicated endpoints unaffected by weighted steering if needed.

sara-oncall: monitoring dashboards: error-rate dropped to 6% after shift, p95 latency back to acceptable but still elevated. Continuing to watch for 30m.

ops-bot: note: oncall handoff scheduled in 45m; leaving a detailed status in #inc-summaries. If AWS confirms route fix, we'll roll traffic back gradually.

maria: Thanks all. Next update in 15. Incident severity set to SEV2. If AWS confirms resolution, we'll run postmortem on root cause and add route propagation checks to runbook.
